 How much more would surviving spouses of veterans get with 3.6% COLA?
 Kayode Crown Wed, November 11, 2026 at 3:33 PM MST 1 min read Surviving spouses of veterans who died on or after Jan. 1, 1993, get at least $1,699 monthly from the Department of Veterans Administration as compensation. The spouses of those who died before that get that as a minimum but may receive more depending on the veteran's military pay grade. 
 If Congress approves the 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment for 2027, the base payment of $1,699 would increase to about $1,761, beginning with the December payment issued Dec. 31. 
 That would be an increase of about $61 a month, adding $734 over the course of one year and bringing the yearly payment from $20,392 to $21,126. 
 Some surviving spouses qualify for additional benefits. A surviving spouse whose veteran held a total VA disability rating for at least eight years before death and who was married to the veteran for those same eight years receives an additional $361 monthly. 
 Each eligible child under 18 adds $421 per month to the benefit. 
 With the 3.6% COLA, those two compensations would increase to about $374 and $436 per month, respectively. 
 A surviving spouse with two surviving children under 18 who also qualifies for the eight-year provision would get a total of at least $3,007 per month in 2027, which would amount to $36,080 over one year, up from $34,827. 
 That is an increase of $1,254 over one year.
